name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two, three or four wheels, a saddle or seat, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts and one brake horsepower, in one of three classes: Class I and Class II (throttle) stop at 20 mph, Class III (pedal assist) at 28 mph. Counted as a bicycle under the Nebraska Rules of the Road.

restrictions.rule: Class I assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class II can power it whether or not the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class III assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Two, three or four wheels, a saddle or seat, and fully operative pedals
Its motor may produce no more than 750 watts and no more than one brake horsepower
A bicycle under the Rules of the Road, with a bicycle's rights and duties
Not a motor vehicle or a motor-driven cycle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
No statewide minimum age for any class
No helmet requirement: the state helmet law covers motorcycles, autocycles and mopeds only
No speedometer or labeling requirement in state law
The state, its agencies and local governments may permit, restrict or ban it on areas they own or control, by regulation or posted signs; riding where it's banned is a Class III misdemeanor

One whose motor exceeds 750 watts or one brake horsepower, or that assists past its class's speed, isn't an electric bicycle: with pedals, an automatic transmission, no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) and a 30 mph design speed it's a moped, which needs an operator's license; otherwise a two-wheeler under 2,238 W or built for off-road use only is a minibike, kept off the streets, and any other a motorcycle needing a Class M license, title and registration. Up to 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), any of them is also a motor-driven cycle
